rejected.title: Joan of Arc
card: Joan of Arc was a peasant girl from France. She said that God had sent her to help France win its war against England. At that time, peasants and women rarely led armies.
In 1429 she led French forces to relieve the besieged city of Orléans. Her leadership lifted French hopes, and soon after she helped lead the king to be crowned.
The English and their French allies captured her. A church court found her guilty, and she was burned to death in 1431.
Later, she came to be seen as a French hero. The Catholic Church made her a saint in 1920.
rejected.remember: A peasant girl's faith and leadership helped France in 1429. She was burned in 1431 and later honoured as a hero and saint.

a.q: Why was Joan of Arc's role in 1429 so unusual for her time?
opts: A peasant girl led armies, saying God sent her
A queen led armies to defend her own kingdom
A priest led armies to defend the Church's lands
A noble knight led armies to take back Jerusalem
a.why: Joan was a peasant girl, and peasants and women rarely led armies then. She led French forces because she said God had sent her. She was not a queen, and her war was against England, not for Jerusalem.
a.clue: Think about who she was and what she said sent her.

b.q: Which event came first in Joan of Arc's story?
opts: She led French forces at Orléans
She was put on trial by a church court
She was burned to death after her trial
She was made a saint by the Church
b.why: Joan led French forces at Orléans in 1429. Her trial and death came in 1431, and she was made a saint much later, in 1920. Her trial did not come before her success in battle.
b.clue: Check the year the card gives for each event.
